## Summary

An arXiv paper (2610.26456, submitted 2026-10-19; Koa, Liu, Li, Feng, Liang, Giroux, Wen, Yao, Huang, Lamarre — NUS/CFM-shaped author list; q-fin.PM + cs.LG) that builds an **interpretable deep-learning ranker for sector rotation**:

- **Task framing:** sector rotation as *ranking* sectors by expected forward risk-adjusted active performance (forward sector-vs-benchmark Sharpe), not point-forecasting returns — matches how benchmark-relative PMs actually allocate overweights/underweights.
- **Architecture (from the OCR'd Figure 1):** (1) fundamental + technical signals represented through **expert-defined temporal characteristics** (per-pillar encoders); (2) **regime conditioning** — signals conditioned on learned latent macro states via **cross-attention** (macro factors gate which signals matter now); (3) **cross-sector self-attention** (sectors modelled jointly, not independently); (4) a ranking head on top.
- **Interpretability is a first-class output:** expected-gradient attributions decompose contributions of individual signal×transformation pairs; macro attention maps and cross-sector attention maps expose the learned conditioning and dependency structure. You can interrogate *why* a sector ranked top this month.
- **Evaluation:** weekly S&P 500 sector data, **2002–2024**, under **combinatorial purged cross-validation** (López de Prado-style leakage control); claims outperformance vs. representative ranking and ML baselines on multiple ranking metrics. Ablations attribute gains to latent macro states, regime conditioning, and cross-sector modelling.

## Why it matters

- This is the *institutional, methods-careful* version of the regime-conditioned rotation idea the vault has been circling all quarter: [[2026-09-09-l1vsun-yield-curve-aware-momentum]] (anonymous AI card, unverifiable) → [[2026-09-09-p123-five-etf-rotation]] (disclosed vendor screen) → [[2026-09-02-pristinecap-techno-fundamental-suite]] (macro-conditioned suite, real but closed) → **this** (full paper: named authors, arXiv ID, purged CV, ablations, attribution diagnostics). Same concept family at the top of the evidence hierarchy.
- The purged cross-validation + ablation discipline is exactly the multiple-testing/leakage hygiene demanded by [[2026-10-24-dmartin-deflated-sharpe-ratio]] and [[2026-10-26-lucasjoly-thesis-ctafutures-trend-research]] — the paper practises what those captures preach.
- Sueppel (macro-synergy.com) is a long-standing systematic-macro research curator; him flagging it is a quality signal, not engagement bait — unlike the L1vsun card, the artifact checks out on every verification gate: real ID, real authors, real abstract, fetchable full text.
- **Skepticism gates:** (1) "outperforms baselines on ranking metrics" ≠ tradable alpha — no net-of-costs, turnover, or capacity discussion in the abstract; a ranking model that beats on rank-correlation can still be uneconomical after sector-swap friction. (2) Ranking metrics under CPCV still involve researcher degrees of freedom (signal set, characteristic definitions, hyperparameters) — deflated-Sharpe-style multiple-testing corrections are not mentioned in the abstract. (3) Weekly sector data 2002–2024 is one market, one regime set (GFC, ZIRP, COVID, hiking cycle) — external validity to other markets unproven. (4) Figure 1 OCR recovered the component labels but garbled some arrow captions — diagram read is approximate; check against the PDF.
- **Not actionable for the personal book:** no sector-rotation pipeline exists here; this is a reference capture for the ML-rotation knowledge thread. If that thread ever turns into a build, this paper is the starting design doc.
